title: Ride dispatcher built on small pluggable interfaces
name: Ride dispatch loop

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how the Dispatcher and NearestIdleStrategy use the interfaces declared in types.ts (return values, nullability, and the DispatchDecision variants)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. MatchingStrategy.choose returns DriverCandidate | null and the dispatcher checks chosen !== null before using it, widening the radius otherwise. Every exit of dispatch returns a valid DispatchDecision variant, describe switches exhaustively with a never check, candidate arrays are readonly so strategies cannot mutate locator results (filter makes a new array anyway), and both time-based decisions read time through the injected Clock rather than Date.now.

choiceQuestions.prompt: radiiKm is [2, 5, 10]. No eligible driver is found at any radius and the request is older than maxRequestAgeMs. What does dispatch return?
choices: It throws because chosen is null
choiceQuestions.explanation: lastRadius is updated on every iteration, so after the loop it is 10; the request is too old to defer, so no_drivers with 10 is returned. Deferral only happens when age < maxRequestAgeMs, 2 would be the first radius not the last, and a null choice just continues the loop.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A new MatchingStrategy is added that prefers premium-rated drivers. Which candidates can it ever be offered by the Dispatcher?
choices: Only candidates whose vehicleClass matches the request, within the current radius
All nearby drivers regardless of vehicle class
Only drivers that have been idle for at least minIdleMs
Only the single nearest driver per radius
choiceQuestions.explanation: Dispatcher filters nearby by vehicleClass before calling choose, so every strategy sees only matching drivers within the radius being searched. The idle filter lives inside NearestIdleStrategy, not the dispatcher, and the full eligible list is passed, not just the nearest.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What is the main benefit of NearestIdleStrategy taking a Clock rather than calling Date.now()?
choices: It makes choose asynchronous so it can await the time source
Tests can fix the current time to check the minIdleMs cutoff deterministically, and it shares one notion of time with the Dispatcher
It prevents drivers with lastTripEndedAt === null from being chosen
It lets the strategy cache ETA results between calls
choiceQuestions.explanation: Injecting Clock makes idle-time comparisons deterministic in tests and consistent with the dispatcher's own age check. choose stays synchronous, null lastTripEndedAt is treated as infinitely idle (eligible), and nothing is cached.
